newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria awards contract to improve access to LNG unit.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria awards contract to improve access to LNG unit.

text.p: Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Co (NLNG) said on Tuesday it had awarded a contract to a Belgium company to improve access to its LNG plant being built in Bonny in the southeast.

Steve Ollerearnshaw, NLNG's British managing director, and his predecessor Dutchman Theo Oerlemans, told a news conference that Dredging International had been awarded a contract to dredge the Bonny river after competitive bids from many firms.

"We have joined forces with oil multinational Mobil Nigeria to finance the dredging of the Bonny river. Both of us will each pay 50 percent of the cost of the project," said Oerlemans, at the conference to formally introduce Ollerearnshaw.
Mobil Nigeria is a joint venture between Mobil Corp and state oil company Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
The new chief executive of the NLNG takes over from Oelermans, who is going to London for a new post with the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
They did not give the cost for the dredging project.
Construction work is proceeding on Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project which is to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of gas per year from 1999.

Dredging International said in a statement on Monday that dredging would commence in April, adding: "The scope of the work requires dredging of up to eight million cubic metres of materials to create a channel depth of about 12.5 metres and a width of 215 metres."
On completion, bigger vessels would also be able to carry associated gas to the LNG plant from Mobil's new gas export project -- Oso II condensate -- expected to come on stream in 1998.
About 600 million cubic feet of associated gas would be produced daily at the Oso II project, which is 51 percent owned by Mobil while state-owned oil company NNPC has the rest.

Ollerearnshaw said there was no question about his company meeting the target date of constructing the LNG plant. "The money is there to do the job, the design work is almost completed and things have started to rise from the ground at the site."

Shell Gas BV is the technical leader with 25.6 percent of the equity in the NLNG joint venture with NNPC which has 49 percent. The other partners are Elf Aquitaine with 15 percent and Italy's Agip with 10.4 percent.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enagas of Spain, Gaz de France and Botas of Turkey.
